title: Jack and the Water That Took a Turn
synopsis: Jack watches a fire engine water demonstration at the open day, tracing the path from the engine tank through its pump and a bent hose to a painted target.
continuity_state: Before: It is the afternoon of the open day. The audience has seen the vehicles and protective clothing. Captain Ann has arranged a controlled water demonstration in the training yard. After: Jack adds a separate water-route sketch to his blue notebook: engine tank, pump, hose, nozzle and painted practice target. Adult crew demonstrate and drain/repack the hose afterward. The park rain gauge and farm-road drainage still have their earlier recorded histories.

related_resources.reason: Supports specific factual descriptions, not story outcome claims.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: "From the tank, through the pump, along the hose, and out the nozzle," Captain Ann said.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Fire-engine water moves from the apparatus tank through a pump into a discharge hose and nozzle.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: The cited public fire-service education, manufacturer, or municipal materials support the precise equipment description, not the fictional events or the effect of listening.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: The hose curved around a corner, but the water still traveled through it.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Flexible hose can route a pumped flow around bends without creating a new source of water; normal bends do not stop the flow.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: The cited public fire-service education, manufacturer, or municipal materials support the precise equipment description, not the fictional events or the effect of listening.

source_note: Original fiction about talking animals and a boy scientist. Public fire-service materials support equipment facts and open-day practices, not the invented event or listener outcomes.
